items.title: [RFC]: Cutting P/D-disaggregation TTFT: first-token seeding, fast KV side channels, and concurrent router dispatch (NixlConnector)
items.body:
### Motivation.

Scope

vLLM V1 engine (NixlConnector P/D path) + vllm-project/router (P/D disaggregated routing)

Summary

On a single-node 3-Prefill / 1-Decode (3P1D) deployment with NixlConnector, the P→D KV handover costs far more in orchestration than in data transfer. Three engine-side changes and one router-side change cut the handover critical path (P emits token#1 → client receives token#1) from ~197ms to ~36ms p50 (measured at --block-size 64 on both ends). Combined with re-tuning the existing --block-size knob from 16 to 64 (no code change; ~263ms → ~197ms on its own), the full recipe yields −23% mean/median TTFT, −10% P99 TTFT, +7% request throughput versus the stock NIXL 3P1D setup at default settings, with no TPOT regression. All changes are flag-gated and fall back to today's behavior.

Problem

Traced on 8×L20 (Qwen3-32B-FP8, TP2, 3P1D, fp8 KV, FlashInfer, ~4.9k-token prompts), the baseline handover breaks down as (p50):
Cost component | p50 ms | Root cause -- | -- | -- D recomputes token#1 after the KV arrives | 58.5 | P already sampled it (max_tokens=1) but the router discards it D worker starts the NIXL pull one step late | 28.8 | Pull metadata rides SchedulerOutput; queues behind the in-flight forward D scheduler learns of completion one step late | 28.1 | Completion rides ModelRunnerOutput; quantized to step boundaries D front-end (HTTP/tokenize/enqueue/schedule) runs after P finishes | 32.2 | Router dispatches the two stages serially NIXL transfer window (~2.5k-token suffix, TP2) | 46.9 | ~33ms pure transfer — the only "real" work — plus 0-28ms of in-window completion-detection quantization (removed by P2 below)
Additionally, with the default --block-size 16 a ~5k-token pull fragments into tens of thousands of ~8KB NIXL descriptors and per-descriptor overhead dominates: the transfer window is ~105ms, and the handover ~263ms. --block-size 64 (FlashInfer's effective page cap) cuts the transfer window by ~58ms; the end-to-end handover drops more (~66ms, to 197ms) because a shorter transfer window also shrinks cross-step alignment effects. We propose documenting this as deployment guidance (Proposal 0, no code change).
### Proposed Change.

Proposed changes

P1 — First-token seeding. P's NixlConnector.request_finished() returns the sampled token in kv_transfer_params.first_token_ids (the router already forwards it opaquely). When D's KV pull completes, the scheduler seeds the token (append_output_token_ids), emits it immediately, and clamps num_computed_tokens so the next forward produces token#2. Removes the ~58ms recompute from TTFT (only the first ITL absorbs the forward). Flag: VLLM_PD_SEED_FIRST_TOKEN.
P2 — Fast KV side channels. Two ZMQ IPC channels between D's EngineCore and its TP workers: (a) fast dispatch — publish reqs_to_recv right after schedule() so a worker listener thread starts the NIXL read immediately; (b) fast notify — a worker poller detects completion within ~0.5ms and pushes to an EngineCore bridge thread, which aggregates TP ranks, seeds token#1 (P1), and writes the output directly to the output queue. Removes both ~28ms step-boundary waits. Flags: VLLM_PD_NIXL_FAST_DISPATCH, VLLM_PD_NIXL_FAST_NOTIFY.
P3 — Concurrent router dispatch + D-side prepare parking. The router dispatches P and D concurrently: D gets a prepare request ({do_remote_prefill: true, remote_ready: false}), tokenizes, enqueues, prefix-matches and allocates blocks ("arms"), then waits in WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS. When P responds, the router POSTs P's kv_transfer_params to a new D endpoint POST /v1/pd_kv_ready; the API server pushes it straight to the P2 bridge thread, which merges the params and fast-dispatches the pull — no step boundary anywhere on the ready→pull path. Lost notifications hit a timeout (VLLM_PD_PREPARE_READY_TIMEOUT_S) and fall into the existing failed-KV-load path (local recompute). Flag: VLLM_PD_CONCURRENT_DISPATCH (router).
P3a — Early-arm as a memory/performance trade-off. Parking without allocating ("late-alloc") gains almost nothing: the step-boundary wait just moves to the ready path (~15ms p50). Allocating at park time ("early-arm") realizes the gain but pins the request's KV blocks for the duration of the prefill (~0.7s at our load). We propose a flag (VLLM_PD_EARLY_ARM) with late-alloc as the memory-constrained fallback.

Results

Handover critical path, p50, same machine/workload (1000 requests):
Configuration | Handover p50 -- | -- Stock NixlConnector, --block-size 16 (default) | 262.6ms --block-size 64 (Proposal 0, existing knob) | 197.1ms \+ P1 + P2 | 63.2ms \+ P3 (late-alloc) | 51.8ms \+ P3a (early-arm) | 35.7ms
Client-visible vs. stock defaults: mean TTFT 863.9ms (−23%), median 783.1ms (−23%), P99 2296.1ms (−10%), throughput 1.23 req/s (+7%), TPOT 30.2ms (unchanged).

References

Baseline: vLLM b17039bc (v0.14.0), router ce2d5133 (v0.1.12).

items.title: [Bugfix] Scale KV page size for hidden states extraction with TP
items.body:
## Summary

- Fixes assertion crash `assert self.page_size_padded >= real_page_size` when using hidden states extraction with tensor parallelism on models with hybrid attention (e.g. `poolside/Laguna-S-2.1`)
- Root cause: TP shards KV heads across ranks, shrinking the target page size, but hidden state per-token cost uses the full unsharded `hidden_size` — the page size assertion fails when `hidden_size > page_size * TP`
- Fix scales up all target group block sizes when hidden-state per-token cost exceeds the common page, before aligning hidden-state specs

## Reproduction

```bash
python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
    --model poolside/Laguna-S-2.1 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
    --speculative-config '{"method": "extract_hidden_states", "target_layer_ids": [2,11,20,30,39,48]}' \
    --port 8000
```

Crashes with:
```
assert self.page_size_padded >= real_page_size
AssertionError
```

## Test plan

- [x] All 73 tests in `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py` pass
- [x] Verified end-to-end: Laguna-S-2.1 with TP=4 + hidden states extraction starts successfully

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Scale UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs groups by DCP
items.body:
## Purpose

#49964 gated the DCP scaling of a group's token span on `isinstance(group.kv_cache_spec, AttentionSpec)` so that Mamba groups stay unscaled. `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` is a container rather than an `AttentionSpec` subclass, so DSA models — whose indexer and MLA layers merge into a single uniform group — lost the DCP factor too:

- `build_offloading_config` reports `tokens_per_block = block_size` (64),
- `resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes` still returns `block_size * dcp` (128) for a single group,

so enabling CPU offload under DCP dies at startup:

```
AssertionError: tokens_per_block=64 not divisible by tokens_per_hash=128.
Hybrid models (e.g. Mamba+Attention) need --enable-prefix-caching to align block sizes.
```

Reported by @Leoyzen on GLM-5.2, TP8/DCP2, `fp8_ds_mla`, MTP, `OffloadingConnector`: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46514#issuecomment-5166406963

The scaling is now keyed off a helper that unwraps the container, so Mamba groups stay unscaled and every attention group keeps its DCP span. Same call site is fixed in `resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes` for multi-group configs.

Related: #50823 fixes the other half of the same container-not-unwrapped family (block table width).

## Test

Three tests, one per call site plus the hybrid case, next to the Mamba tests from #49964:

- `offloading_connector/test_config.py::test_dcp_scales_uniform_type_attention_group_blocks`
- `offloading_connector/test_config.py::test_dcp_scales_uniform_type_group_alongside_mamba`
- `core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_resolve_block_sizes_scales_uniform_type_group_by_dcp`

Verified fail→pass in a container built from the current nightly (`0.26.1rc1.dev255+g5e35a6f4f`); each test fails on unpatched `main` with the reported assert (`tokens_per_block=16 not divisible by tokens_per_hash=32`) or a wrong span, and the two suites pass with the fix:

```
python3 -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py -q
# 115 passed
```

Config-level change, no effect on model output; no eval run.

AI assistance (Claude) was used for this work; all changes reviewed.

items.title: [Bugfix] MiniMax-M3 fp8_e5m2 KV cache on SM80 (A100/A800): admit the format Triton can read, fix the CUDA-graph KV corruption
items.body:
Draft port of the SM80 fp8-KV enablement for MiniMax-M3 onto current main. Fixes #50881.

**In this draft already:** the Triton attention backend guard now admits `fp8_e5m2` on SM80 — Triton there can read fp8e5; it is only fp8e4nv (e4m3) that needs SM89+. e4m3 stays rejected below SM89, and the error now suggests `fp8_e5m2` to Ampere users instead of a bf16 downgrade.

**Coming with hardware verification on 8xA800 (tomorrow):**
- route dense-layer KV writes through the CUDA `reshape_and_cache_flash` (software fp8 convert) instead of the Triton kernel that needs native fp8e4nv;
- make `MiniMaxM3SparseAttention._insert_kv` CUDA-graph-safe via `@eager_break_during_capture` — the root cause of the fp8+graph garbage diagnosed in #50881;
- the remaining SM89 guards on this path, plus needle/1M-window/GPQA numbers re-measured on main.

Diagnosis, per-kernel numerical probes, and the fork-based patch set this ports from: https://github.com/Hakureirm/minimax-m3-ampere

Marked draft until the full set and the on-hardware verification land.

items.title: [Bug]: MiniMax-M3 fp8 KV cache on SM80 (A100/A800): coherent with --enforce-eager, garbage under CUDA graphs — root cause + working fix
items.body:
### Your current environment

- 8x A800-80GB (SM80, no native fp8 tensor cores), TP=8
- Model: MiniMax-M3-AWQ-INT4 (weight-only int4)
- Launch: `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e5m2 --max-model-len 1048576 --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --block-size 128 --enable-chunked-prefill`
- Findings below were made on a community M3 fork; mainline shares the `_insert_kv` KV-write path this report is about. Full container env available on request.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Trying to run MiniMax-M3 with an fp8 KV cache on A100/A800 fails two different ways:

1. `fp8` (e4m3): Triton refuses outright — `type fp8e4nv not supported in this architecture`. SM80 can only read `fp8_e5m2` (same conclusion as #3965).
2. `fp8_e5m2`: the server boots, takes a 1M-token window, and generates pure garbage.

The garbage is **not** an fp8 precision problem. We measured the e5m2 write/read kernels on SM80 directly: round-trip error 4.5%, full-kernel 12–16% — normal for a 2-mantissa-bit format. The decisive experiment:

- `--enforce-eager`: output is perfectly coherent (but 5.2 tok/s — unusable for an 8-TP MoE);
- any CUDA-graph mode: garbage.

Root cause: the bf16 path writes KV through a fused CUDA op, which is graph-safe. The fp8 path goes through `MiniMaxM3SparseAttention._insert_kv` — plain Python that allocates a fresh tensor and does an advanced-index scatter (`idx_cache[slot_mapping] = ...`). Under graph capture that write corrupts the index-K cache, the sparse indexer picks the wrong top-k blocks, and attention reads the wrong KV. This one mechanism explains all three observations (bf16+graph fine, fp8+graph garbage, fp8+eager fine).

Fix that works: decorate `_insert_kv` with `@eager_break_during_capture` (the codebase's own idiom for exactly this), route dense-layer KV writes through the CUDA `reshape_and_cache_flash` (software fp8 convert), and relax the SM89 guards to SM80. With that, on 8xA800:

- full 1,048,576-token window fits (fp8 halves KV; pool ~1.22M tokens);
- coherent output; needle retrieval hit at ~100k depth; an 840k-token prompt prefills clean;
- ~86 tok/s decode, ≈90% of the bf16 baseline — on SM80 fp8-KV buys memory, not speed;
- GPQA Diamond, one harness against both the official API and this build: 93.4% vs 90.9% — quantization costs ≈2.5 pts.

Patches, per-kernel probes, and the eval writeup: https://github.com/Hakureirm/minimax-m3-ampere. (#39137's over-broad e5m2 gate is already fixed on main by #45040 — thanks for that.)

I am porting the patches onto current main and will open a PR tomorrow. Filing the diagnosis first in case it saves someone the same hunt — and in case a maintainer knows a reason the `eager_break_during_capture` route is wrong here, better before the PR than after.

items.title: [BugFix][Kernel] Pass kv_cache_dtype as int to avoid stable-ABI host leak
items.body:
## Purpose

Fix the host-memory leak on the eager `reshape_and_cache_flash` path reported in #50150.

Root cause is upstream PyTorch stable-ABI: every eager call that unboxes a `str` into `std::string` allocates host memory that is not freed (pytorch#190493; fixed on PyTorch main, still present on the wheels vLLM commonly ships with). This op takes `kv_cache_dtype` as `str` and is dispatched eagerly, so long-running servers grow RSS.

**Mitigation:** keep the Python API as `CacheDType` strings, map them to a dense `int` code before the stable ABI boundary, change the C++ schema/`ops.h` signature to `int64_t`, and resolve the dtype name on a small stack table inside the kernel wrapper. Call sites go through `ops.reshape_and_cache_flash`, which owns the mapping.

**Not a duplicate:** searched open PRs for `#50150`, `reshape_and_cache_flash` host leak, and stable-ABI string leak. No open PR implements this mitigation. Issue #50150 has an interest comment but no assignee and no competing PR.

## Test Plan

```bash
# Unit: code table / mapper / coverage of CacheDType
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_kv_cache_dtype_code.py -q

# Kernel reshape path (sm_120 binary, RTX 5060 Ti)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py -q \
  -k "reshape_and_cache_flash or kv_cache_dtype"

# Manual ABI + numerical smoke on sm_120 with Docker-built _C (CUDA 13):
# - wrapper "auto" → max_diff_k/v = 0.0
# - direct int code 0 matches wrapper
# - schema rejects str; rejects invalid code 999
```

## Test Result

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `test_kv_cache_dtype_code.py` | **7 passed** |
| ABI schema | `str` rejected (`Expected int`); int accepted |
| Invalid code `999` | clear C++ error |
| Numerical smoke `auto` on sm_120 | **PASS** `max_diff_k=0.0 max_diff_v=0.0` |
| `test_cache.py` reshape filter | **372 passed**, 24 failed (**all `nvfp4`**, NaN diffs) |

The nvfp4 failures look unrelated to the ABI change (dtype code `15` still maps to `"nvfp4"`); they appear to be NVFP4/path/hardware limitations on this build. Non-nvfp4 reshape paths, including the leaky `auto` path, pass.

pre-commit on commit: ruff, typos, clang-format, SPDX, signoff — all passed.

## Notes

- Human-reviewed and tested end-to-end; AI assistance used while drafting the change.
- Does not change model token outputs; host-side API of one custom op only. No model evals.
- Public Python still takes string `kv_cache_dtype`; only the stable-ABI custom op uses int codes.

Fixes #50150

items.title: [V1][Scheduler] Clamp KV connector match to the prompt suffix
items.body:
## Summary

`Scheduler.schedule()` can crash with a bare `AssertionError` when a KV connector is attached and prefix caching produced a local hit:

- `assert num_new_tokens > 0` (scheduler.py ~914) when the connector's match plus the local hit reaches the end of the prompt (zero local tokens left for the prefill step), or
- `assert num_computed_tokens <= request.num_tokens` (scheduler.py ~832) when the match plus the local hit *exceeds* the prompt length.

The local prefix lookup already caps hits at `num_tokens - 1` (`get_computed_blocks`, kv_cache_manager.py:259) because the last token must always be recomputed to obtain logits — and the async-load promotion path applies the same rule ("on a full prompt hit, we need to re-compute the last token", scheduler.py ~2671). The connector-reported external match was the only unbounded input: it is added to the local hit without being clamped to the remaining prompt suffix.

This is reachable through vLLM's own test connector: `MockKVConnector` returns a fixed `matched_tokens` regardless of the local hit (tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/utils.py), and any connector match of `M` tokens on top of a local hit `L` trips the asserts whenever `L + M >= num_tokens`. The same code exists in upstream `main` (both asserts, no clamp).

## Fix

In the prefill branch of `Scheduler.schedule()`, clamp the connector match to the prompt suffix that is not locally cached, mirroring the `num_tokens - 1` cap of the local lookup:

```python
num_external_computed_tokens = min(
    num_external_computed_tokens,
    max(request.num_tokens - num_new_local_computed_tokens - 1, 0),
)
if num_external_computed_tokens == 0:
    load_kv_async = False
```

- At least one token of local prefill remains, so `num_new_tokens > 0` holds.
- `num_computed_tokens <= num_tokens` holds; the `num_tokens - 1` bound matches the documented "recompute the last token" rule.
- When the clamp leaves nothing to load, `load_kv_async` is cleared so the async-load assert (`num_external_computed_tokens > 0`) stays satisfiable.
- `connector_prefix_cache_hits` (stats) now records the clamped value actually used.

No behavior change when the connector reports a legal match: the clamp only reduces matches that would overrun the prompt.

## Tests

Two regression tests in `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py` cover both failure faces (each fails with `AssertionError` before the fix, passes after):

- `test_connector_match_clamped_to_prompt_suffix` — a match that reaches the end of the prompt (zero local tokens) is clamped to the remaining suffix minus one; the request then decodes normally.
- `test_connector_match_exceeding_prompt_clamped` — a block-aligned local hit plus a longer match would exceed the prompt; the match is clamped and the request finishes prefill.

Commands and results:

```
# regression tests fail without the fix (stashed scheduler.py):
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_connector_match_clamped_to_prompt_suffix tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_connector_match_exceeding_prompt_clamped -q
# -> 2 failed (AssertionError inside Scheduler.schedule())

# with the fix:
# -> 2 passed

# full scheduler test file (incl. 66 connector/kv/prefix-cache/throttle tests):
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q -p no:cacheprovider
# -> 139 passed, 16 warnings in 229.93s
```

No model-affecting change: this only bounds token accounting at scheduling time; sampling/output paths are untouched, so no model eval is needed.

## AI assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance (opencode). The submitting author reviewed every line and ran the tests above.

Not a duplicate: searched open PRs/issues for connector match clamping / `get_num_new_matched_tokens` bounds / the two asserts — nothing open addresses this.

items.title: [Docs][KV Connector][NIXL] Document NIXL KV connector stats semantics
items.body:
## Summary

Completes the remaining source-level documentation items (1-3) of #41230: explain what the NIXL \`KV Transfer metrics\` log line and the NIXL Prometheus metrics mean, with a focus on the multi-rank (TP > 1) aggregation semantics that previously caused user confusion.

Covers:

- \`NixlKVConnectorStats\` - per-interval telemetry container: what each \`data\` key holds, its units, and the pooling (never per-rank averaging) semantics of \`aggregate\`.
- \`record_transfer\` - per-transfer telemetry from NIXL: \`xferDuration\` (end-to-end, posting + data movement) and \`postDuration\` (time to submit the transfer to the RDMA backend), both converted from microseconds to seconds; bytes and descriptor counts stored as-is.
- \`clone_and_reset\` / \`is_empty\` / \`num_successful_transfers\` - the snapshot-and-reset contract, and why failure-only intervals are intentionally kept so they still reach the logger and Prometheus.
- \`reduce\` - definitions of every field in the log line: mean/P90 durations in ms, MiB conversion (bytes / 2**20), aggregate throughput (total MiB / sum of transfer durations, not wall-clock), descriptor mean, and the all-zeros path when no transfer succeeded.
- \`NixlPromMetrics.observe\` - histogram vs counter recording per engine.
- \`KVConnectorLogging.observe\` / \`log\` - the scheduler-sync vs logging-interval distinction and the accumulator lifecycle.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

- #44055 (merged) covered item 4 only - the user-facing docs page (\`docs/features/nixl_connector_usage.md\`); its changed files were limited to that page. Maintainer markmc confirmed items 1-3 (source-level documentation in \`stats.py\` / \`metrics.py\`) remain open (2026-06-12).
- No open PR touches these two files for documentation purposes. Commenters on #41230 (ammmanism, kritikagarg, dhariskhan1275) expressed interest, but no PR had been opened for items 1-3.

## Test commands and results

Docs-only change - no behavior change, so no model evaluation applies (no effect on output, accuracy, or serving).

- \`ruff check\` on both changed files: all checks passed.
- \`git diff --check\`: clean; all lines within the 88-char limit.
- \`python -m compileall\` on both files: OK.
- Documented semantics verified against the actual \`reduce\` / \`aggregate\` / \`is_empty\` logic with a standalone script: pooled mean/P90 math, MiB conversion, the \`num_successful_transfers == 0\` guard, and the failure-only zero path - all assertions passed.

## AI assistance disclosure

This PR was developed with AI assistance (opencode) and reviewed by a human. The AI helped draft the docstrings; every documented statement was then traced to its code path (\`_pop_done_transfers\` -> \`record_transfer\` -> \`get_kv_connector_stats\`/clone_and_reset -> \`KVOutputAggregator.aggregate\` -> scheduler merge -> \`KVConnectorLogging.observe\`/log + \`NixlPromMetrics.observe\`) and cross-checked against the semantics documented in #44055. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and verified the claims before submission.

items.title: Fix OverflowError in prompt_logprobs when external KV pre-fills prompt
items.body:
When an external KV connector (PD disagg / LMCache / NIXL) advances num_computed_tokens past local-computed, _get_prompt_logprobs_dict ships an unfilled LogprobsTensors.empty_cpu tensor; the stale int32 then overflows u32 in tokenizer.decode -> OverflowError, crashing the engine.

Only ship the logprobs tensor when there is something to fill (num_logits > 0).

Closes #50792




## Purpose

In a PD-disaggregated (or any external-KV-connector) setup, a request with `prompt_logprobs` crashes the decode engine with `OverflowError: out of range integral type conversion attempted`.

`prompt_logprobs` needs per-position logits, which come from running the prompt forward. When an external KV connector (Mooncake / NIXL / LMCache) pre-fills the prompt KV, `num_computed_tokens` advances to `prompt_len`, so the engine skips the prompt forward and has no logits for the prompt positions.

In `_get_prompt_logprobs_dict` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py`), the last-chunk branch ships the logprobs tensor *before* checking whether there is anything to fill:

```python
else:  # last-chunk branch
    num_logits = num_remaining_tokens          # 0 / -1 because num_computed >= N-1
    completed_prefill_reqs.append(req_id)
    prompt_logprobs_dict[req_id] = logprobs_tensors   # ships the tensor
if num_logits <= 0:
    continue                                   # skips the copy_ that fills it
```

The tensor is created by `LogprobsTensors.empty_cpu` with `torch.empty(dtype=torch.int32)` (uninitialized). Since the request is remote-prefilled, this is the first and only entry into the function, so the tensor is shipped without a single `copy_`. The local prefix-cache path is not affected because `skip_reading_prefix_cache=True` (auto-set when `prompt_logprobs` is enabled) forces a local recompute from position 0; the external connector path does not honor this flag, so `num_computed_tokens` still jumps to `prompt_len`.

                 # This is the last chunk of prompt tokens to return.
                 num_logits = num_remaining_tokens
                 completed_prefill_reqs.append(req_id)

+                    prompt_logprobs_dict[req_id] = logprobs_tensors
```

Manual reproduction on a PD-disaggregated setup (1 prefiller + 1 decoder + example proxy) with a `prompt_logprobs=1` non-streaming request.

## Test Result

| Setup | `prompt_logprobs` | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| PD disagg (P+D) | yes | `OverflowError`, engine crash | no crash, request returns |
| PD disagg (P+D) | no | no crash | no crash (unchanged) |
| Single engine, no external connector | yes | no crash | no crash (unchanged) |

Before the fix, the decoder logs:

```
ERROR [async_llm.py:704] AsyncLLM output_handler failed.
File ".../vllm/v1/engine/async_llm.py", line 675, in output_handler
File ".../vllm/v1/engine/output_processor.py", line 648, in process_outputs
File ".../vllm/v1/engine/logprobs.py", line 352, in update_from_output
    self._update_prompt_logprobs(output.new_prompt_logprobs_tensors)
File ".../vllm/v1/engine/logprobs.py", line 147, in _update_prompt_logprobs
    else convert_ids_list_to_tokens(
File ".../vllm/v1/tokenizers/detokenizer_utils.py", line 100, in convert_ids_list_to_tokens
    token_str = tokenizer.decode([token_id])

    text = self._tokenizer.decode(token_ids, skip_special_tokens=...)

After the fix, the decoder no longer ships the unfilled tensor; `new_prompt_logprobs_tensors` is absent so `_update_prompt_logprobs` skips it, the engine stays alive, and the request returns normally.

items.body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text - vllm: 0.23.0 (reproducible on main) - Platform: Ascend NPU (PD disagg with external KV connector) - Python: 3.12 ``` ### 🐛 Describe the bug
## 🐛 Describe the bug In a PD-disaggregated setup, sending a request with `prompt_logprobs` to the decode engine crashes the engine with `OverflowError: out of range integral type conversion attempted`. ### Root cause `prompt_logprobs` needs per-position logits, which come from running the prompt forward. But when an external KV connector (Mooncake/NIXL/LMCache) pre-fills the prompt KV, `num_computed_tokens` is advanced to `prompt_len`, so the engine skips the prompt forward and has no logits. In `_get_prompt_logprobs_dict` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py`), the last-chunk branch ships the logprobs tensor *before* checking whether there's anything to fill: ```python else: num_logits = num_remaining_tokens # 0 (or -1) because num_computed >= N-1 completed_prefill_reqs.append(req_id) prompt_logprobs_dict[req_id] = logprobs_tensors # ships the tensor if num_logits <= 0: continue # skips the copy_ that would fill it ``` The tensor is created by `LogprobsTensors.empty_cpu` with `torch.empty(dtype=torch.int32)` (uninitialized). Since the request is remote-prefilled, this is the first and only entry, so it's shipped with no `copy_` ever run. The API server then decodes every id via `tokenizer.decode`, and a negative stale int32 overflows the `u32` conversion in the Rust tokenizer, raising `OverflowError`. The local prefix-cache path is protected because `skip_reading_prefix_cache=True` (set when `prompt_logprobs` is enabled) forces a local recompute from position 0. The external connector path does not honor this flag, so `num_computed_tokens` still jumps to `prompt_len`. ### Minimal reproduction Two vllm engines (1 prefiller, 1 decoder) + the example disagg proxy: **Prefiller:** ```bash vllm serve --port 8100 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --max-model-len 8192 --enforce-eager \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnectorV1","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_port":"30000"}' ``` **Decoder:** ```bash vllm serve --port 8200 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --max-model-len 8192 --enforce-eager \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnectorV1","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_port":"30100"}' ``` **Proxy** (`vllm-ascend` `examples/disaggregated_prefill_v1/load_balance_proxy_server_example.py`): ```bash python load_balance_proxy_server_example.py \ --prefiller-hosts 127.0.0.1 --prefiller-ports 8100 \ --decoder-hosts 127.0.0.1 --decoder-ports 8200 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8090 ``` **Trigger** (non-streaming — vllm rejects `stream=True` + `prompt_logprobs>0`): ```bash curl http://127.0.0.1:8090/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "model":"", "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello, introduce yourself in Chinese"}], "max_tokens":200,"temperature":0,"prompt_logprobs":1,"stream":false}' ``` ### Observed error (decoder log) ``` ERROR [async_llm.py:704] AsyncLLM output_handler failed. File ".../vllm/v1/engine/async_llm.py", line 675, in output_handler File ".../vllm/v1/engine/output_processor.py", line 648, in process_outputs File ".../vllm/v1/engine/logprobs.py", line 352, in update_from_output self._update_prompt_logprobs(output.new_prompt_logprobs_tensors) File ".../vllm/v1/engine/logprobs.py", line 147, in _update_prompt_logprobs else convert_ids_list_to_tokens( File ".../vllm/v1/tokenizers/detokenizer_utils.py", line 100, in convert_ids_list_to_tokens token_str = tokenizer.decode([token_id]) File ".../vllm/v1/tokenizers/hf.py", line 86, in decode File ".../transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py", line 1032, in _decode text = self._tokenizer.decode(token_ids, skip_special_tokens=...) OverflowError: out of range integral type conversion attempted ``` The APIServer then shuts down. ### Control experiments | Setup | `prompt_logprobs` | Result | |---|---|---| | PD disagg (P+D) | no | no crash | | PD disagg (P+D) | yes | **D crashes with OverflowError** | | Single engine, no external connector | yes | no crash | So the crash requires both an external KV connector and `prompt_logprobs`. DCP/MTP/memcache are not required (reproduced without them). ### Suggested fix In `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` (main @ 5672), only ship the tensor when there's something to fill: ```diff else: # This is the last chunk of prompt tokens to return. num_logits = num_remaining_tokens completed_prefill_reqs.append(req_id) - prompt_logprobs_dict[req_id] = logprobs_tensors + if num_logits > 0: + prompt_logprobs_dict[req_id] = logprobs_tensors ``` ### Expected behavior A `prompt_logprobs` request should not crash the engine when an external KV connector pre-fills the prompt KV. With the fix above the engine no longer ships an unfilled logprobs tensor; a companion proxy-side change (to be filed against vllm-ascend) returns real prompt_logprobs by harvesting them from the prefiller. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bug]: CUDA graph memory profiler charges an mnbt-linear profiling transient as "graph memory" → KV cache pool −18–24% on hybrid GDN models since v0.26.0 (the real FULL graphs cost ~24 MiB each)
items.body:
## Summary

Since v0.26.0, `profile_cudagraph_memory()` reports ~4.2 GiB of "CUDA graph
memory" on a hybrid-GDN model (Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, int4 AutoRound, SM120) where
0.23.x reported 0.56 GiB for the *same graph set* (PIECEWISE=7, FULL=5). The
KV cache pool shrinks by the difference: **1,489,281 → 1,135,957 tokens
(−23.7%)** on 0.26.1 nightly, −17.9% on v0.26.0, with identical config.

Root cause (evidenced below): **~96% of the reported number is not graph
memory.** It is the allocator high-water mark of the estimator's *first FULL
sample*, the only sample that runs `profile_seq_lens =
min(max_model_len, max_num_batched_tokens // num_tokens)` — a warmup+capture
whose total profiled context across the batch equals `max_num_batched_tokens`.
That forward transiently allocates **~128 KiB per batched context token** on
0.26.x (it did not on 0.23.x), and the measurement — a free-memory delta with
no `empty_cache()` between samples — charges the whole transient as CUDA
graph memory and sizes the KV pool down by it.

The real captures are innocent: with the new
`--profiler-config '{"capture_torch_profiler": true, ...}'` tracing, the
largest single allocation in any of the 12 real graph captures is **11.8
MiB**, and the estimator's own per-graph increments are 14–26 MiB.

⚠️ **A one-sided fix is dangerous** — see "Why this must be fixed as a pair"
below. On this model the mischarged 4 GiB currently doubles as activation
headroom that the memory profiler fails to attribute to the GDN long-prefill
path; releasing it to the KV pool (e.g. `cudagraph_mode: PIECEWISE`, or
`VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=0`) produces a reproducible OOM
crash in `chunk_gated_delta_rule` on a single 32k prefill.

- GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation (96 GB, SM120), TP=1

| 131072 | 16384 | **2,070 MiB** | 2.12 GiB | 1,490,081 |

Exactly linear in mnbt (~128 KiB per batched context token), independent of
max_model_len. Consistent with `profile_seq_lens = mnbt // num_tokens` making
**total profiled context = num_reqs × (mnbt / num_reqs) = mnbt**. A separate
config on the same GPU with mnbt=2048 (NVFP4 sibling model) reports 0.61 GiB.

## Evidence 3 — capture traces: real captures allocate nothing big

`--profiler-config '{"profiler":"torch","torch_profiler_dir":"/traces","capture_torch_profiler":true}'`
traced all 12 real captures (trace for `capture_16_FULL` attached in a comment below; the other
11 available on request). Largest single allocation in ANY capture:
**11.8 MiB** (`aten::empty`); per-capture allocation totals 0.5–2.0 GiB of
small transients that the shared pool overlays across graphs. The real
capture path (`capture_model` → `_capture_cudagraphs`) never passes
`profile_seq_lens`.

The runtime "actual" figure is `start_free − end_free` spanning **all
warmups + captures + vision-encoder graph capture, measured before the
post-capture `empty_cache()`** — so warmup transients cached in the allocator
are counted as graph residency. Estimate and "actual" agree (0.4% diff)
because they mismeasure the same way, not because the graphs hold 4 GiB.

## Evidence 4 — the estimator didn't change; the model-side forward did

I diffed the two images file-by-file: `profile_cudagraph_memory`,
`_warmup_and_capture`, `profile_seq_lens` plumbing, `cuda_graph.py`
(pool sharing), `cudagraph_dispatcher.py`, and the GDN
`build_for_cudagraph_capture` are **byte-identical** between 0.23.1 dev714
and 0.26.1rc1.dev245 (modulo a ROCm stream fix and the new profiler hooks).
dev714 runs the same profile-seq-lens sample and reports 0.5 GiB.

So the ~128 KiB/context-token transient is a 0.23→0.26 regression in the
model-side decode-with-context path executed by that sample (the window
includes the FLA move to `vllm/third_party/flash_linear_attention`, the
`mamba/gdn/` package refactor, and new ops like `gather_initial_states`). I
did not pin the exact op: the capture profiler doesn't cover the estimator
phase. Wrapping `profile_cudagraph_memory()` with
`torch.cuda.memory._record_memory_history()` should name it in one run.

## Why this must be fixed as a pair (data from the v0.26.0 evaluation)

On v0.26.0 I tested the obvious mitigations:

- `cudagraph_capture_sizes: [1,2,4,8,16]`: 4.15 GiB — trimming graphs is not
  the lever (consistent with per-graph ≈ 24 MiB).
- `cudagraph_mode: PIECEWISE`: reports 0.11 GiB, KV pool grows to 1,546,269 —
  and then the engine **OOM-crashes on a single 32k-token prefill**:

  ```
  vllm/third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/wy_fast.py, recompute_w_u_fwd
      w = k.new_empty(B, T, H, K)
  torch.OutOfMemoryError: Tried to allocate 458.00 MiB. GPU 0 ... 121.00 MiB free
  ```

- `VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=0`: same failure mode, silently.

The memory profiler measures peak activation at 8.29 GiB for this config, but
the real GDN chunked-prefill peak is ~4 GiB higher. The mischarged
"cudagraph" reservation currently absorbs that gap by accident. Therefore:

1. **Accounting fix** — don't charge profiling/warmup transients as CUDA
   graph memory (measure retained pool after `empty_cache()`, or isolate the
   profile-seq-lens sample from the graph-memory figure); **and**
2. **Profiling fix** — make the activation-peak profiling actually cover the
   hybrid (GDN) chunked-prefill worst case, so the freed memory is reserved
   for the reason it is actually needed.

Fixing (1) alone converts this from a −24% KV pool regression into an OOM
crash for GDN hybrids at long prefill. (3) Optionally, finding and removing
the new ~128 KiB/token allocation fixes the estimate at the source and
probably improves real decode-with-long-context memory behavior too.

## Reproduction

Any GDN hybrid at a non-trivial mnbt shows it; no load needed:

```bash
# boot with VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG and read the two
# "Estimated {PIECEWISE,FULL} CUDA graph memory" lines:
#   FULL first-capture ≈ 128 KiB × max_num_batched_tokens, per-graph ~24 MiB
# halve --max-num-batched-tokens → FULL first-capture halves, KV pool jumps
```

## Related

- #44740 — sibling defect in the same measurement (negative estimates on
  unified memory): both stem from free-memory deltas spanning warmup+capture
  with allocator caching in between; the open fixes there (#44745, #46932)
  address the sign error, not this transient mischarge.
- #30515 — the PR that introduced cudagraph memory profiling (the estimator
  logic itself is fine; it is measuring a forward that got 100× more
  allocation-hungry).

items.title: [Core] Extensible (growable) KV cache
items.body:
> **Stacked on #44458** (`lwilkinson/kv-layout/core-standardize`). Only the commits above that PR's head belong to this one; review #44458 first.
> This is a **draft** — it cannot merge until #44458 lands, after which the base will be retargeted to `main`.

## Summary

Opt-in growable KV cache (`--enable-extensible-kv-cache`) built on the standardized KV cache layout from #44458.

vLLM sizes the KV cache from a profiling run, then allocates it up front. Any memory the engine consumes *after* profiling — CUDA graph pools, the spec-decode logits all-gather, workspace growth — has to be guessed at via
headroom margins, and a wrong guess is either an OOM or wasted HBM.

This change reserves virtual address space for the KV cache capacity but commits physical pages incrementally (CUDA `cuMem*` / ROCm `hipMem*`):

1. Allocate the VA reservation, commit one block per layout segment.
2. Run warmup and CUDA graph capture.
3. Measure *actual* post-warmup free memory and re-size.
4. `extend_kv_cache()` maps the remaining pages under the same base pointer.

Because each block keeps a fixed offset within its layout segment and the base pointer never moves, captured graphs and layer views stay valid across the growth — no re-view, no re-capture.

### What #44458 buys this

The layout standardization removes most of what made the earlier version of this work invasive. Buffer segmentation is now a pure function of `KVCacheLayout.stride_order` (new `num_outer_segments()` helper) instead of per-backend shape/stride/block-dim probing; connector registration views are a plain `narrow(0)` of the logical `[B, H, N, C]` view; and the packed / `block_stride` special cases disappear entirely. The integration is ~30%
smaller than the equivalent against `main`.

### Views are authoritative, not `storage.nbytes()`

The one contract change worth reviewer attention. Under an extensible cache the untyped storage spans the **reserved** capacity, of which only each view's per-segment block prefix is physically backed. Any code deriving block geometry or registration extents from `untyped_storage().nbytes()` will compute a size that includes unbacked pages.

Updated accordingly, with the contract documented on `KVConnectorBase_V1.register_kv_caches`:

- `NixlBaseConnectorWorker.register_kv_caches` — collects per-region committed spans and registers those; falls back to the single per-allocation registration when the storage is fully backed. Block-major packing is
  detected from view strides rather than `nbytes()`.
- `get_kv_cache_block_regions` (`v1/worker/utils.py`) — same, which also covers the CPU-offload connector.

KV-transfer init is deferred until after `extend_kv_cache`, so connectors only ever register committed memory. On the NIXL path, extend also defragments (release + single-chunk recommit per segment): UCX cannot transfer a VMM region spanning multiple `cuMemCreate` handles.

## Relationship to existing work

- **#47363** (@zhuohan123, "Demo implementation of extensible kv cache memory)  — this is the productionization of that demo, not a competing implementation. It adds the V1 + V2 runner integration, the measured post-warmup sizing pass, VMM probe/fallback, sleep-mode support, KV connector support, and a ROCm backend. Happy to fold this into #47363 instead if that's preferred.
- **#44458** — strictly a dependency; no overlap in changed behavior.
- Searched open PRs for extensible/growable/VMM KV cache work; nothing else overlaps.

Contributors: @zhuohan123 (original demo), @zjy0516 (packed-storage bounding, sleep gate).

## Testing

Unless noted, run against this branch at its current head.

**Unit** — `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py tests/utils_/test_extensible_tensor.py tests/v1/engine/test_engine_args.py -v` → 29/29 pass (GB200, aarch64).

**e2e, 1×GB200, CUDA graphs on** — outputs byte-identical to a non-extensible baseline for: standard generation, sleep(level=1)/wake, and `--kv-cache-memory-bytes`.

**e2e, sizing under pressure** — Qwen3.5-4B TP4, MTP `num_speculative_tokens=100`, chunk 256, `gpu-memory-utilization=0.92` (a config that OOMs without this change): passes in both eager and cudagraph modes. Sizing 35,277→34,721 tokens (eager), 35,243→34,592 (cudagraph). Functional check 64/43 answers correct.

**e2e, NIXL P/D disaggregation** — Qwen3-0.6B, HND, block 128, gsm8k via P/D proxy:

| config | gsm8k | expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1P1D eager | 0.422 | ~0.41 |
| 1P1D cudagraph | 0.418 | ~0.41 |
| P(TP1)→D(TP2) | 0.415 | ~0.41 |
| P(TP2)→D(TP2) | 0.415 | ~0.41 |

**Model evaluation** — the feature is opt-in and does not change model outputs; the byte-identical-output comparison above and the gsm8k table are the evidence for that.

### Known gaps

- The V2 encoder-cache profiling reservation (last commit) is validated on the equivalent branch against `main` (Qwen2-VL-2B: 16,384-token budget reserved, 238,148 blocks committed) but **has not been re-run on this branch** — the cluster battery above has no multimodal configuration. Will re-run before marking ready.
- No unit coverage for `commit(defragment=True)` or the connector sleep gate; both are exercised only by the e2e NIXL runs. Adding these before ready.
- Multi-node NIXL (NIC RDMA path with the GDR + POSIX-FD allocation flags) is unvalidated; the repro harness is localhost-only.
- The ROCm `hipMem*` backend is written but untested on AMD hardware.
- Encoder-decoder mixed layouts raise rather than falling back.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change: for the port onto the #44458 layout model, the connector geometry audit, and drafting. I have reviewed every changed line, and ran the tests and cluster validation above
myself.

items.title: [Bug]: int8_per_token_head KV with prefix caching DISABLED corrupts the FIRST generated tokens (Gemma-4 hybrid, Triton, idle KV pool)
items.body:
## Environment
- vLLM v0.26.0, V1 engine, Model Runner V1
- 2× RTX 3090 (Ampere/sm86), TP=2, no NVLink (`--disable-custom-all-reduce`)
- Model: `cyankiwi/gemma-4-31B-it-AWQ-4bit` (Gemma-4 31B, hybrid attention: 50 sliding layers head_dim 256 + 10 global head_dim 512)
- `--attention-backend=TRITON_ATTN --kv-cache-dtype=int8_per_token_head --no-enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill --kv-sharing-fast-prefill --max-num-seqs=48 --max-model-len=16384`
- Same rig as #49716 / #50158 / #50159 / #50702.

## Summary

With `int8_per_token_head` KV **and prefix caching turned off**, the first few generated
tokens are corrupted, while the rest of the (2–3.5k token) response is perfectly coherent
and well-formed. This happens at **~3% KV pool utilization** — no flood, no preemptions,
no memory pressure of any kind.

This is **not** #50702. There the corruption needs the pool pinned at ~100% with continuous
block eviction/reuse, and prefix caching **on**. Here the pool is nearly empty and prefix
caching is **off**. The only thing the two share is int8 KV.

It is also **not** quantization quality loss: the same int8 config with prefix caching
**enabled** is clean on the same inputs (see the factorial below). Precision loss cannot
depend on whether a cache is enabled.

## Evidence: full 2×2 factorial, n=48 per arm

Same 48 request bodies in every arm (captured verbatim from our production traffic:
system+user, ~4.2k chars prompt, `temperature=0.6`, `max_tokens=8800`, output is a strict
JSON object whose first key is `dominant_theme`). Endpoint is **first-key damage**, i.e.
the response's first key is missing, mangled, or not `dominant_theme`.

| Arm | KV dtype | prefix caching | first-key damage | of which silent | rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **V1** | `int8_per_token_head` | **off** | **6 / 48** | 1 | **12.5%** |
| V2 | `auto` (bf16) | off | 0 / 48 | 0 | 0.0% |
| V3 | `int8_per_token_head` | on | 0 / 48 | 0 | 0.0% |
| V4 | `auto` (bf16) | on | 0 / 48 | 0 | 0.0% |

V1 vs any single control arm: Fisher exact two-tailed **p = 0.0265**.
V1 vs the pooled controls (0/144, same run, same box, same bodies): **p = 0.00019**.
Clopper-Pearson 95% CI: V1 **4.7–25.2%**, controls **0–2.5%** (non-overlapping).

An earlier independent run with n=24 gave 4/24 = 16.7%, consistent with the above.

**Only the intersection is dirty — the defect requires int8 AND no-prefix-caching together.**

## Corruption signature

All damage is confined to the first ~12 bytes of the response; everything after is valid.
Four distinct shapes observed (each from a different request):

```
{\n: "Развитие эмоционального интеллекта…      key name gone entirely, colon left behind
{\n": "Организация и запуск малого бизнеса…    key name gone, its CLOSING quote survived
{\n{\n  "dominant_theme": "Выбор и эксплуат…   stray extra brace
{\n  "dominant": "Информационная безопасно…    key name truncated  <-- parses fine!
```

The last shape is the **silent** variant: `json.loads` succeeds, so a consumer's schema
lookup just silently misses the field. Any check that only counts parse failures will
undercount this bug — and, worse, will not measure it in the control arms at all.

Note the second shape: for `{\n": ` to be emitted, the key's contents must vanish while its
closing quote survives. That is hard to explain as sampling.

## Repro

1. Boot the config above (`int8_per_token_head` **plus** `--no-enable-prefix-caching`).
2. Send long-ish prompts (~1.5k tokens) that force a structured output beginning with a
   fixed key, at modest concurrency (we used 6). No flood needed; our KV pool sat at ~3%.
3. Inspect the **first key** of each response — do not rely on `json.loads` alone, or the
   silent variant is invisible.
4. Flip either lever back (`--kv-cache-dtype=auto`, or drop `--no-enable-prefix-caching`)
   and the damage disappears.

We hit this in production: enabling `--no-enable-prefix-caching` (as a workaround for
#50702) took a consumer from ~1 such case per month to ~120 per hour, and reverting it
returned the rate to zero within minutes.

## Hypothesis (unverified)

Speculative, offered only as a starting point. The damage is localized to the tokens
generated immediately after the prompt, which suggests the boundary between prefill and
the first decode step — specifically the prompt's **last, partially-filled block**. With
per-token-head int8 scales, appending the first decoded token into that partial block may
recompute or overwrite scales covering the prompt tokens already resident in it, so the
earliest decode steps dequantize recent context against wrong scales and recover once
generation moves into freshly allocated blocks. Prefix caching changes how that final
partial block is allocated and handed out, which would explain why enabling it masks the
issue.

If that is the right area, the rate should depend on whether the prompt length is a
multiple of the block size — we have not tested that, and are happy to.

## Notes

We can run experiments on this hardware on request (the rig is dedicated and we already
have a captured-traffic replay harness with the first-key detector). Related: #50702
(int8 × prefix-cache reuse at pool saturation) — different trigger, possibly the same
underlying scale-handling code.

items.title: [Bugfix][Core] Fix invalid block handling for hybrid KV cache groups
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #50687.

Invalid-block recovery assumed that each request had exactly one KV cache group:

```python
(req_block_ids,) = self.kv_cache_manager.get_block_ids(req_id)
```

With the hybrid memory allocator, `get_block_ids()` returns one block ID list per KV cache group. As a result, KV load failure recovery raised the following exception for requests using multiple groups:

```text
ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 1)
```

This PR removes the single-group assumption and updates invalid-block recovery to:

* Search for invalid blocks across all KV cache groups.
* Compute each invalid block's token boundary using the corresponding group's block size.
* Align recomputation to a common scheduler block boundary.
* Collect downstream eviction candidates across all KV cache groups when eviction is required.

The regression tests cover:

* An invalid block reported from a non-primary KV cache group.
* A mixed block-size configuration with group sizes of 16, 32, and 64.
* Alignment from an invalid block boundary at token 96 to the common scheduler boundary at token 64.

The KV connector test utility now accepts a separate `hash_block_size`, allowing tests to represent configurations where the hash, group, and scheduler block sizes differ.

## Test Plan

Run the invalid-block and KV load failure tests:

```bash
pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_cache_pollution_prevention.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_error_propagation.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_invalid_blocks_correctness.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py \
  --disable-warnings
```

Run the existing hybrid and Mamba scheduler tests:

```bash
pytest -q \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  -k "hybrid or mamba" \
  --disable-warnings
```

Run checks on the modified files:

```bash
pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/utils.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_invalid_blocks_correctness.py
```

## Test Result

Before the fix, the new multi-group regression test failed with:

```text
ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 1)
```

After the fix:

```text
19 passed, 15 warnings
3 passed, 134 deselected, 14 warnings
```

The regression tests verify that:

* An invalid block in the second KV cache group is handled without an exception.
* The request is rescheduled from the correct recomputation boundary.
* Mixed KV group block sizes of 16, 32, and 64 are handled correctly.
* An invalid block beginning at token 96 is aligned to the common scheduler boundary at token 64.

All pre-commit hooks passed.

No documentation update is required because this change does not alter any user-facing API, configuration, or documented workflow.

## AI Assistance Disclosure

This change was developed with AI assistance. Every modified line was reviewed, and the implementation was validated by @jiyujung.

items.title: [PD] Emit inactive KV blocks for decode affinity
items.body:
Publish GPU block inactivity when the last request reference is released so external schedulers can maintain accurate decode load signals.


## Purpose

Add a new KV cache event, `BlockInactive`, so external PD schedulers can track when a GPU prefix-cached block is no longer actively referenced.

Today, KV event consumers can observe `BlockStored` and `BlockRemoved`, but cannot reliably detect that the last request released a block while it may still remain in the prefix cache. Without a refcount-zero signal, decode-affinity load accounting (`active_blocks`) tends to only increase or needs fragile heuristics.

This PR:

- Adds `BlockInactive` to `KVEventBatch`, emitted from `BlockPool.free_blocks()` when `ref_cnt` drops to 0 for a hashed GPU block (`medium=MEDIUM_GPU`).
- Publishes it through the existing KV event path (`take_events()` / ZMQ). No new scheduler-loop wiring.
- Gates emission for Prefill-only instances: `kv_role == "kv_producer"` still emits `BlockStored` / `BlockRemoved`, but does **not** emit `BlockInactive`, so Prefill frees do not pollute decode load signals.
- Decode (`kv_consumer`), union (`kv_both`), and non-PD setups continue to emit Inactive via `KVTransferConfig.should_emit_block_inactive` (`kv_role != "kv_producer"`).

Related issue: #50730 

## Test Plan


pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  -k "free_blocks_emits_block_inactive or free_blocks_skips_block_inactive or kv_transfer_should_emit_block_inactive" \
  -q

Coverage:

free_blocks emits BlockInactive when enable_block_inactive_events=True.
Prefill-style gate (enable_block_inactive_events=False) still emits BlockStored, but not BlockInactive.
KVTransferConfig.should_emit_block_inactive is False for kv_producer, True for kv_consumer / kv_both / default.

## Test Result
Unit tests above pass locally.
Existing BlockStored / BlockRemoved behavior is unchanged.
Old KV event consumers can ignore the unknown BlockInactive type.
Validated end-to-end in a 1P1D (one Prefill + one Decode) setup. Additional tests are still in progress.

items.title: [Feature]:  Emit BlockInactive KV events when GPU block ref_cnt drops to zero
items.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

## Feature

Add a new KV cache event type, `BlockInactive`, published when a GPU prefix-cached block's `ref_cnt` drops from 1 to 0 in `BlockPool.free_blocks()`.

This is distinct from existing events:

- `BlockStored`: block becomes actively referenced / stored
- `BlockRemoved`: block is physically evicted from memory
- `BlockInactive` (proposed): block still resides in GPU memory, but no request currently references it

## Motivation

In PD-disaggregated serving, an external scheduler (e.g. a KV-aware router / load balancer) may track per-decode-worker active KV occupancy for decode-node selection, for example:

load_score = (query_block_len - overlap_depth) + active_blocks

Today, consumers can observe BlockStored / BlockRemoved, but they cannot reliably detect that the last request released a block while it may still sit in the prefix cache. Without a refcount-zero signal, active_blocks tends to only increase, or requires fragile heuristics.

I'm working on decode-affinity routing for PD clusters and need a clean, engine-native signal for "GPU block is no longer actively referenced."

## Proposed behavior
In BlockPool.free_blocks(), when ref_cnt == 0, enable_kv_cache_events is on, and the block has a hash, append BlockInactive(block_hashes=..., medium=MEDIUM_GPU).
Publish via the existing KV event path (ZMQ / take_events()). No new scheduler-loop wiring.
Role gate: Prefill-only instances (kv_role == "kv_producer") still emit BlockStored / BlockRemoved, but do not emit BlockInactive, so Prefill frees do not pollute decode load signals. Decode (kv_consumer), union (kv_both), and non-PD setups continue to emit Inactive.
Gate with kv_role != "kv_producer" (do not use is_kv_producer, which includes kv_both).
Rough mapping to ref_cnt:

0 -> 1           BlockStored
N -> N+/-1 (>0)  (no new event)
1 -> 0           BlockInactive (proposed)
eviction         BlockRemoved (unchanged)
I have a draft implementation on a fork and can open a PR after discussion. It adds BlockInactive in kv_events.py, gates emission via KVTransferConfig.should_emit_block_inactive, and adds unit tests in tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py.

_No response_
